questions.stem: According to the passage, about how many hours a day do many working-age Americans spend in front of screens?
questions.evidence: An estimated 104 million Americans of working age spend more than seven hours a day in front of screens
questions.explanation_ko: 1억 400만 명의 미국 성인이 하루 7시간 넘게 화면 앞에서 보낸다고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following has NOT been shown to be caused by blue light exposure from screens?
questions.evidence: exposure to blue light from digital screens has not been shown to cause permanent eye damage
questions.explanation_ko: 청색광이 영구적인 눈 손상을 일으킨다는 것은 입증되지 않았다고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about products such as blue light glasses, based on the passage?
options: They are the most effective way to prevent nearsightedness.
Changing screen habits may matter more than these products for reducing eye strain.
They are required by eye doctors for all patients.
They work only for children, not adults.
questions.evidence: The group says it is how people use digital devices that causes problems, not the blue light coming from screens.
questions.explanation_ko: 문제의 원인은 청색광 자체가 아니라 기기 사용 방식이라고 했으므로, 특수 안경보다 사용 습관을 바꾸는 것이 더 중요할 수 있다고 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author include Steven Reed's comparison of eye strain to holding a light weight over your head for hours?
options: To explain why eye muscles get tired even from a task that seems easy
To recommend a specific exercise routine
To criticize people who use computers too much
To describe how eye surgery works
questions.evidence: it's like picking up a light weight and trying to hold it over your head for hours
questions.explanation_ko: 이 비유는 가벼워 보이는 일도 오래 지속하면 눈 근육이 피로해질 수 있음을 설명하기 위한 것입니다.

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "engaging with" mean in "most children are engaging with screens throughout the day"?
questions.evidence: most children are engaging with screens throughout the day
questions.explanation_ko: engaging with은 여기서 화면을 사용하거나 상호작용하고 있다는 뜻입니다.

blanks.sentence_ko: 그는 그런 문제를 겪는 사람들에게 안과 검진을 받고 화면을 보는 중간에 규칙적으로 휴식을 취하라고 권한다.
가벼운 물건이라도 오랫동안 들고 있으면 몸은 결국 지치게 된다고 그는 덧붙였다.
너무 많은 화면 시청이나 가까운 물체에 집중하는 것은 특히 아이들에게서 근시의 진행을 빠르게 할 수 있다.
"비록 그것이 크게 힘든 일은 아니지만, 몸은 결국 지치게 됩니다,"라고 그는 덧붙였다.

key_points: Many working-age Americans spend more than seven hours a day looking at screens, which can cause dry eyes, blurry vision, headaches, and nearsightedness, especially in children.
Blue light from screens has not been proven to cause permanent eye damage, and eye strain from screens is temporary.
Eye doctors recommend the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
Blue light glasses have not been shown to be very effective; the real cause of eye strain is how people use their devices, not blue light itself.
Turning off screens one to two hours before bed and lowering screen brightness can help people sleep better.
main_idea: Spending long hours looking at digital screens can cause several eye and sleep problems, but simple habits like taking regular breaks and limiting screen time before bed can help reduce the strain.
restate_sentence: Too much screen viewing can lead to dry or watery eyes, unclear vision and headaches.
